questions.question: When driving down a long or steep hill, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for fast traffic behind you.
Assume all traffic is moving at the same speed.
Look over your shoulder for traffic behind you.
Press your brake pedal hard to control traffic speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for fast traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for vehicles moving quickly toward you when driving down hills or mountains. Vehicles go faster on steep slopes. Watch for large trucks and buses that may be speeding.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, reduce your speed without using the brake and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when returning to the road.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, which technique helps avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highways as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive on your vehicle.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not needed.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and black markings. Drivers must follow all regulatory signs. Where this sign is posted, passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other cars.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your vehicle and others. This gives you time to react to mistakes other drivers make.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Careless handling can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. For serious bleeding, use direct pressure to slow the blood flow.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. However, let pedestrians and other traffic that are still in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be ready for?

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind from the large vehicle.
Vehicle parts falling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction you must drive on this street. You can only drive in the direction shown.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks other traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks other traffic
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can block normal traffic flow and is illegal. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
Can see directly behind your vehicle.
Can see in your rearview mirror.
Can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic first.
May drive through if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. Always let other vehicles and pedestrians go first when turning.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must always let pedestrians cross first at any intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle coming on a divided highway. You should:

options.text: Ignore it if other lanes are open.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move over to clear the way, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move over to clear the way, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down and move your vehicle to create space for the emergency vehicle. Then stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What is a key trait of a defensive driver?

options.text: Anticipation
Passivity
Easy to distract
Anger

questions.correctAnswerText: Anticipation
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers think ahead about what might happen on the road. They keep a safe distance from other cars and take action to avoid problems.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus dropping off children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch carefully for children walking along the road. Always drive slowly and carefully around children.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse an alcohol test?

options.text: Your license will be suspended.
It is your right and nothing will happen.
It is recommended.
You will go to jail for one night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive, you agree to take an alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, your license will be suspended for one year on the first offense. For a second or later offense, your license will be suspended for two years.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires work less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
When you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires work less well.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires can push water away. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane. Hydroplaning means your car slides on water instead of gripping the road.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol levels above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol levels above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol will reduce your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will get worse. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the right air pressure.
Replace tires that are worn down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tire tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: When an oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Do not try to squeeze between the car and the bicycle at the same time. Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep empty space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles next to you on the left and right.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up right away.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: Louisiana law requires headlights to be used:

options.text: When the driver is tired.
Between sunset and sunrise.
When the temperature drops below freezing.
During daytime in good weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Louisiana law requires your headlights to be on between sunset and sunrise. You must use low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or following another vehicle within 200 feet.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Signs of road rage include:

options.text: Deliberately blocking other vehicles.
Flashing headlights.
Cutting off or swerving in front of other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Road rage includes deliberately blocking other drivers, tailgating, flashing headlights, cutting off or swerving in front of drivers, pursuing another vehicle, threatening others, and using rude gestures. If you see road rage, give the driver space and do not fight back.
